title: Exactness of ordinary scalar extension with its counit-normalized shift
statement: Fix a prime l, finite extensions E and L of Q_l and a Q_l-algebra map ι:E→L. Let T be a scheme in the same universe as the coefficient fields. Let C=completedDerivedScalarExtension l E L ι T be ordinary derived change of completed coefficient rings [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. For any coherent integer shift structure e on C satisfying completedScalarShiftOrdinaryNormalization [def-fd-completed-scalar-shift-representative-property], C with precisely e is a triangulated functor. No constructibility, completeness, dimension or invertibility condition on T is needed.

proof.text: Apply ordinary derived change of rings to the actual completed coefficient map. The homotopy-level termwise tensor functor preserves shifts and cones. Its everywhere-defined left derived functor is triangulated. Keep its canonical counit-compatible shift.

On each flat-term K-flat complex P its counit is invertible. The counit square solves for the derived shift component uniquely. The supplied ordinary normalization is the same square with the standard tensor and Q shift isomorphisms; cancel the shifted counit to identify its component with the canonical one.

Every derived object has a flat-term K-flat representative. Naturality transports the component equality to every object. Consequently both shift structures give the same image triangle, so exactness for the canonical shift gives exactness for e.

theorem completedScalarOrdinary_normalized_exact
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L]
    (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L) (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u})
    (e : (completedDerivedScalarExtension l E L ι T).CommShift ℤ)
    (he : completedScalarShiftOrdinaryNormalization ι T e) :
    (fun [_s : (completedDerivedScalarExtension l E L ι T).CommShift ℤ] ↦
      (completedDerivedScalarExtension l E L ι T).IsTriangulated) (_s := e)
